description: Type design rules for TypeScript/JavaScript projects - encapsulation, invariants, usefulness, and enforcement

rules.description: Use private fields for internal state
rules.message: Consider using private fields to encapsulate internal state
rules.design_check: Do the proposed class designs expose internal state as public fields? Consider making internal state private with accessor methods. Flag for review.

rules.message: Avoid exposing mutable collections - return copies or use readonly
rules.design_check: Do any proposed types expose mutable collections (arrays, sets, maps) as public fields? Use readonly or return copies to prevent unintended mutation. Flag for correction.

usefulness.description: Rules for type usefulness and ergonomics

rules.message: Deeply nested types are hard to use - extract intermediate types
rules.design_check: Do any proposed type/interface designs have more than 3 levels of nesting? Extract intermediate named types for clarity. Flag for correction.

rules.message: Avoid 'as any' - use proper type guards or fix the type
Avoid non-null assertion (!) - use optional chaining or type guards instead

strict_mode.description: TypeScript strict mode enforcement — ensures code follows strict type-checking practices and does not bypass the type system

rules.description: Use @ts-expect-error instead of @ts-ignore for type suppression
rules.message: Use @ts-expect-error instead of @ts-ignore — it will error when the suppressed issue is fixed, preventing stale suppressions
rules.fix_suggestion: Replace @ts-ignore with @ts-expect-error and add a description of the expected error

rules.description: Never disable type checking for an entire file
rules.message: Do not use @ts-nocheck — fix type errors individually instead of disabling the entire file
rules.fix_suggestion: Address individual type errors with @ts-expect-error or proper type fixes

rules.description: Avoid double type assertion (as unknown as T) to bypass type safety
rules.message: Double type assertion 'as unknown as T' bypasses all type safety — fix the underlying type mismatch instead
rules.fix_suggestion: Use proper type guards, generics, or fix the type relationship instead of double-asserting

rules.description: Limit use of definite assignment assertion (!:) which bypasses strictPropertyInitialization
rules.message: Definite assignment assertion (!:) bypasses strictPropertyInitialization — initialize in constructor or provide a default value
rules.fix_suggestion: Initialize the property in the constructor, provide a default value, or make it optional with '?:'

rules.description: Avoid type assertion to empty object type which bypasses type safety
rules.message: Avoid 'as {}' or 'as object' — these bypass type safety similar to 'as any'
rules.fix_suggestion: Use a proper interface, 'unknown' with type guards, or fix the type relationship

rules.description: TypeScript projects must have strict mode enabled in tsconfig.json
rules.message: Enable 'strict: true' in tsconfig.json for comprehensive type safety
rules.design_check: Does the design specify TypeScript strict mode (strict: true in tsconfig.json)? Ensure this is enabled for the project. Flag if not mentioned.

dimensions.description: Four dimensions of type design quality (from pr-review-toolkit)

encapsulation.description: How well types hide implementation details

invariants.description: How well types enforce business rules and constraints

usefulness.description: How ergonomic and self-documenting types are

enforcement.description: How well types are enforced at runtime boundaries
